changeSummary: Zero Trust decision prompt v21: the model judges each request from its context. System text: the mission (sign-in, permissions and fixed rules cannot tell a stolen account or an insider from legitimate work), reading the evidence, competing explanations, the four responses, honesty; no decision rule, threshold, floor or later enforcement. User prompt: the v20 dictionary blocks, facts titled RECORDS AND COMPARISONS without the core's conclusions. Output contract v4: action, hypotheses, reasonCodes, reason, riskScore, confidence, mitre; the response check asks again only for a broken format, a wrong citation or a second analysis ESCALATE. v21.1-v21.5: unrecorded is unknown; the owner's records weigh legitimate work against insider misuse; an approval or ticket is a person's earlier judgment; host checks, target scope and past record counts are host or computed facts. v21.6-v21.8: ESCALATE hands the request to the second analysis, with the same facts. v21.9-v21.14 (agent requests): the agent apart from the account; the delegation by its fields; its objective, call arguments, past record targets and case memory as untrusted texts; the token; the agent's session and baseline; record authors and holders; the coverage after the delegation records; a confirmed request. v21.15 (RL-2, RL-4, RL-6): delegation and company policy can cover the work as records; the delegation line states its quantity limits; a code for a request exceeding the delegation's objective; unsupported reason codes cause no second answer. v21.16 (RL-10): an agent on its own states its sponsor's standing delegation. v21.17 (M10A): the system text says whose hand-over a delegation's proof is. v21.18 (CQ-1): a host may tell where call argument values came from; one first seen in a tool's output is a fact line, its sentence also an untrusted text; reason code VALUE_FROM_UNTRUSTED_OUTPUT. v21.19 (BR-C6): a past record line states how the record was learned and which arguments came from a tool's output.
